questions.question: The Eighth five year plan was finally launched in _______ after the initiation of structural adjustment policies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Eighth Five Year Plan** was finally launched in **1992** after the initiation of structural adjustment policies.
 
• The plan period was from **1992 to 1997**.
 
• It marked a significant shift in economic policy with a focus on **liberalization, privatization, and globalization**.
 
• The plan aimed at achieving an average annual growth rate of **5.6%**.
 
• Key areas of focus included **human development, modernization of industries, and infrastructure development**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The structural adjustment policies were initiated in **1991** as part of the economic reforms to address the balance of payments crisis.
 
• The reforms included measures like **deregulation, reduction of import tariffs, and opening up to foreign investment**.
 
• The Eighth Five Year Plan was instrumental in **transforming the Indian economy** and integrating it with the global economy.
 
• It was the first plan to be prepared after the dismantling of the Soviet Union, which had a significant impact on India's economic policies.
 
• The plan emphasized on **enhancing productivity, improving quality of products, and increasing competitiveness** in the global market.

questions.question: In a capitalist society the goods produced are distributed among people ______.

options.text: only on the basis of what people need
on the basis of what people need and on the basis of Purchasing Power
not on the basis of Purchasing Power
not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a capitalist society, goods are distributed **not on the basis of what people need but on the basis of Purchasing Power**.
 
• Purchasing Power refers to the financial ability of individuals to buy goods and services.
 
• This system often leads to inequalities where those with higher purchasing power can afford more goods and services, while those with less purchasing power may struggle to meet their basic needs.
 
• The principle of distribution based on purchasing power is fundamental to the functioning of a capitalist economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Capitalism is an economic system where private individuals or businesses own capital goods.
 
• The production of goods and services is based on supply and demand in the general market (market economy), rather than through central planning (planned economy or command economy).
 
• In capitalist economies, the prices of goods and services are determined in a free price system set by supply and demand.
 
• Key characteristics of capitalism include private property, capital accumulation, wage labor, voluntary exchange, a price system, and competitive markets.
 
• Critics of capitalism argue that it can lead to economic inequality, exploitation, and social injustice.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**79-122**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Articles **79-122** of the Indian Constitution deal with the Indian Parliament.
 
• The Indian Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses, namely, the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• Article **79** establishes the Parliament of India, while Article **80** deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha, and Article **81** outlines the composition of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Subsequent articles cover various aspects related to the functioning, powers, and procedures of the Parliament.
 
• The Parliament is a key legislative body that enacts laws, scrutinizes the government, and represents the interests of the citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Parliament of India** plays a crucial role in the legislative process and ensures the implementation of constitutional provisions.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Indian Parliament has been instrumental in shaping the country's laws and policies to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of Indian Constitution is related to the Fundamental Duties?

__
 
• **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution is related to the Fundamental Duties of citizens.
 
• It was added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• The Fundamental Duties enshrined in Article 51A serve as a reminder to Indian citizens that they have responsibilities in addition to rights.
 
• These duties emphasize the importance of upholding the spirit of patriotism and to support the unity of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Article 51A specifically lists out the duties that every citizen of India is expected to perform.
 
• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties aims to balance individual rights with collective responsibilities.

questions.question: _______ is a state or condition in which an individual or community lacks the financial resources and essentials for a minimum standard of living.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poverty**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poverty** is a state or condition in which an individual or community lacks the financial resources and essentials for a minimum standard of living.
 
• It is a multifaceted concept, which includes social, economic, and political elements.
 
• Poverty can be measured in terms of income level, but it also encompasses a lack of access to basic needs such as food, shelter, education, and healthcare.
 
• Addressing poverty often requires a combination of economic growth, social policies, and targeted interventions to support vulnerable populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Poverty is one of the primary challenges faced by many countries and is a key focus of global development efforts.
 
• The United Nations has set specific goals to reduce poverty through initiatives like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly Goal 1: No Poverty.
 
• Various factors such as unemployment, lack of education, and social exclusion contribute to the perpetuation of poverty.
 
• Effective poverty alleviation strategies often involve improving access to education, healthcare, and employment opportunities.

• Swaminathan's vision for the 'Evergreen Revolution' includes the integration of modern technology with traditional farming practices.

questions.question: Who among the following was associated with the Young Bengal Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Derozio**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Henry Derozio** was a poet and teacher of Anglo-Indian descent, and he is considered the founder of the Young Bengal Movement.
 
• The Young Bengal Movement was a group of radical Bengali free thinkers emerging from Hindu College, Calcutta, in the early 19th century.
 
• Derozio inspired his students to question traditional beliefs and embrace modern and rational ideas, leading to significant social and educational reforms.
 
• The movement played a crucial role in the Bengal Renaissance, promoting progressive thinking and secularism.

 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Henry Thomas Colebrooke** was a British Orientalist and a scholar of Sanskrit and Indian law, but he was not associated with the Young Bengal Movement.
 
• **Charles Wood** was a British politician known for the Wood's Despatch of 1854, which laid the foundation for the education system in India, but he was not involved in the Young Bengal Movement.
 
• **William Jones** was a British philologist and a founding figure of the Asiatic Society of Bengal, known for his work in linguistics and oriental studies, but he was not part of the Young Bengal Movement.
 
• The Young Bengal Movement was characterized by its emphasis on rationalism, liberty, and social reform, significantly influencing the intellectual landscape of Bengal and India.

questions.question: In May 2023, Praveen Sood, the Director General of Police in Karnataka, has been appointed as the next director of the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In May 2023, Praveen Sood, the Director General of Police in Karnataka, has been appointed as the next director of the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**.
 
• The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is the premier investigating agency of India, operating under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.
 
• The CBI is responsible for investigating a wide range of criminal cases, including corruption, economic crimes, and other high-profile cases.
 
• Praveen Sood's appointment comes at a crucial time when the CBI is involved in several high-stakes investigations across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) was established in 1941 as the Special Police Establishment to investigate bribery and corruption in transactions with the War & Supply Department of India during World War II.
 
• In 1963, it was renamed and reconstituted as the CBI by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• The CBI operates under the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
 
• The agency is headquartered in New Delhi and has several regional offices across India.
 
• The CBI is often called upon by the Supreme Court and high courts to investigate high-profile cases.
 
• The CBI director is usually appointed for a fixed tenure of two years.
